questions.q: What does "multi-tenant" mean in the context of public cloud providers like AWS, Azure, and GCP?
options: Each customer gets their own dedicated physical datacenter
The same physical hardware and datacenters serve many different customers, kept isolated by virtualization
Only government agencies are allowed to use the service
Customers must share login credentials with each other
questions.explain: Public cloud is multi-tenant: many customers share the same underlying physical infrastructure, isolated from each other by the hypervisor layer.

questions.q: What distinguishes private cloud from public cloud?
options: Private cloud infrastructure is dedicated to a single organization, whether it's on-premises or hosted by a vendor
Private cloud is always cheaper than public cloud
Private cloud cannot run virtual machines
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Private cloud means the infrastructure is reserved for one organization only, unlike the shared, multi-tenant model of public cloud.

questions.q: What technically makes a deployment "hybrid cloud" rather than just using two separate unrelated systems?
options: Using any two different software products together
On-premises and public cloud infrastructure connected over a private link, such as ExpressRoute or a site-to-site VPN
Running the same application in two different public cloud regions
Having employees who work both remotely and in an office
questions.explain: True hybrid cloud connects on-premises and public cloud infrastructure over a private, dedicated connection so workloads can communicate securely.

questions.q: Which of these is a real, concrete reason a company might choose a hybrid cloud setup?
options: They haven't decided which single cloud provider to use yet
A regulation requires certain data to stay within a specific location or jurisdiction
Hybrid cloud is always required by law for every company
There is no real reason to ever choose hybrid cloud
questions.explain: Compliance and data-residency requirements are a genuine, common driver for keeping some data on-premises while using public cloud for other workloads.

questions.q: In the bank example from this lesson, why does the core transaction database stay on-premises while the web application runs in Azure?
options: Because Azure cannot run databases
Because the ExpressRoute connection is too slow for databases
Because data-residency requirements keep the regulated data on-premises, while the web app still benefits from the cloud's scalability
Because on-premises databases are always cheaper than cloud databases
questions.explain: The database stays on-prem to satisfy compliance requirements, while the customer-facing application still gets the scalability benefits of running in Azure, connected securely via ExpressRoute.
